en.t: 355 ml whole milk
355 ml heavy cream
150 g granulated sugar
10 cm piece vanilla bean, slit lengthwise and seeds removed, pod reserved
4 large egg yolks (≈72 g)

1. Position a strainer over a medium bowl set in a larger bowl containing ice water. Heat the milk, cream, 120 ml of the sugar, and the vanilla seeds and pod in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally to break up the vanilla seeds, until steam appears and the milk is warm (about 80 °C), about 5 minutes.

2. Meanwhile, whisk the yolks and remaining 59 ml sugar in a medium bowl until combined and pale yellow. Whisk half the warm milk mixture into the beaten yolks, 120 ml at a time, until combined. Whisk the milk-yolk mixture into the warm milk in the saucepan; set the saucepan over medium heat and cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until steam appears, foam subsides, and the mixture is slightly thickened or an instant-read thermometer registers 80 to 85 °C. (Do not boil the mixture, or the eggs will curdle.) Immediately strain the custard into the bowl set in the ice bath; cool the custard to room temperature, stirring it occasionally to help it cool. Cover and refrigerate until an instant-read thermometer registers 5 °C or lower, at least 3 hours or up to 24 hours.

3. Add the vanilla extract, if using, and stir well. Pour the custard into the ice cream machine canister and churn, following the manufacturer’s instructions, until the mixture resembles soft-serve ice cream. Transfer the ice cream to an airtight container, press plastic wrap flush against the surface, cover the container, and freeze the ice cream until firm, at least 2 hours. (The ice cream will keep for up to 2 days.)

1. Strednú misu postavíme do väčšej misy s ľadovou vodou a položíme na ňu sitko. V strednom hrnci na strednom ohni zohrievame mlieko, smotanu, 110 ml cukru a vanilkové semienka so strukom; občas premiešame, aby sa semienka rozptýlili, kým sa nezačne pariť a mlieko nie je teplé (asi 80 °C), asi 5 minút.

2. Medzitým v strednej mise metličkou vyšľaháme žĺtky so zvyšnými 53 ml cukru, kým sa nespoja a nezosvetlia. Do rozšľahaných žĺtkov postupne po 120 ml zašľaháme polovicu teplého mlieka. Zmes mlieka a žĺtkov vlejeme za stáleho šľahania k teplému mlieku v hrnci; hrniec postavíme na stredný oheň a za stáleho miešania varechou varíme, kým sa nezačne pariť, pena nezmizne a zmes mierne nezhustne, prípadne kým teplomer s rýchlym odčítaním neukáže 80 až 85 °C. (Zmes nesmie zovrieť, inak sa vajcia zrazia.) Krém hneď precedíme do misy v ľadovom kúpeli; necháme ho vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu a občas premiešame, aby rýchlejšie chladol. Prikryjeme a necháme v chladničke, kým teplomer neukáže 5 °C alebo menej, aspoň 3 hodiny a najviac 24 hodín.

Zmrzlinu preložíme do vzduchotesnej nádoby, na povrch pritlačíme potravinovú fóliu, nádobu zakryjeme a zmrzlinu necháme v mrazničke stuhnúť, aspoň 2 hodiny. (Zmrzlina vydrží najviac 2 dni.)

en.v: 2840 ml stainless steel saucier; whisk; ice cream maker; non-reactive, freezer-safe container

en.t: 265 g plain or very lightly toasted sugar
35 g cornstarch
1/2 plus 1/8 tsp (2.5 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt, or more to taste; for table salt, use about half as much by volume or the same weight
565 g best quality whole milk, preferably grass-fed, divided
225 g best quality heavy cream, preferably grass-fed

1. Whisk sugar, cornstarch, and salt together in a saucier. When no lumps of cornstarch remain, add exactly 396 g of the milk and whisk to combine. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly but not vigorously, until it begins to simmer. This will take about 6 minutes; if the process seems to be moving slowly, simply turn up the heat. When the mixture comes to a boil, set a timer and continue cooking and whisking for exactly 1 minute. This ensures the cornstarch is fully hydrated.

2. Immediately transfer mixture to a large bowl, then whisk in the remaining milk and cream. Bearing in mind that the gelato will taste substantially less sweet once frozen, season with an additional pinch of salt, if desired. Cover and refrigerate the gelato base until cold, thick, and no warmer than 4 °C, about 3 hours (this process can be sped along with an ice bath if time is of the essence; in that case, a stainless steel bowl will help cool the base even faster).

3. Churn in an ice cream maker according to the manufacturer’s directions. Meanwhile, place a 1000 ml container and flexible spatula in the freezer. When gelato looks fluffy and thick, shut off the machine and, using the chilled spatula, scrape gelato into the chilled container. Cover with plastic wrap pressed directly against the surface of the gelato, and freeze until thick enough to scoop, about 4 hours.

4. Gelato is typically served at about -10 °C, while most American freezers run at -18 °C; for the most authentic presentation, soften gelato to -10 °C in the refrigerator before serving. In a squat container, like a yogurt tub or a square storage container, this will take about 45 minutes. The timing will vary substantially depending on the size, shape, and material of the container (such as a metal loaf pan or glass baking dish), so check on the gelato frequently to ensure it does not melt.

1. V hrnci so zaobleným dnom metličkou premiešame cukor, kukuričný škrob a soľ. Keď v zmesi nezostanú žiadne hrudky škrobu, pridáme presne 396 g mlieka a metličkou premiešame. Na strednom ohni za stáleho, no nie prudkého šľahania zohrievame, kým zmes nezačne vrieť. Trvá to asi 6 minút; ak to ide pomaly, jednoducho zvýšime oheň. Keď zmes zovrie, nastavíme časovač a za stáleho šľahania varíme presne 1 minútu. Škrob tak úplne napučí.

2. Zmes hneď preložíme do veľkej misy a zašľaháme zvyšné mlieko a smotanu. Keďže zmrazené gelato bude chutiť výrazne menej sladko, môžeme ho ešte dochutiť štipkou soli. Základ prikryjeme a necháme v chladničke, kým nie je studený, hustý a nemá viac ako 4 °C, asi 3 hodiny (ak sa ponáhľame, proces urýchli ľadový kúpeľ; misa z nehrdzavejúcej ocele pomôže základ vychladiť ešte rýchlejšie).

3. Vymrazíme v zmrzlinovači podľa návodu výrobcu. Medzitým dáme do mrazničky 1000 ml nádobu a pružnú stierku. Keď je gelato nadýchané a husté, vypneme stroj a vychladenou stierkou ho vyškrabeme do vychladenej nádoby. Na povrch gelata pritlačíme potravinovú fóliu a necháme ho v mrazničke, kým nie je dosť tuhé na naberanie, asi 4 hodiny.

4. Gelato sa zvyčajne podáva pri teplote asi -10 °C, zatiaľ čo väčšina mrazničiek má -18 °C; pre najautentickejší výsledok ho pred podávaním necháme zmäknúť v chladničke na -10 °C. V nízkej nádobe, napríklad v kelímku od jogurtu alebo štvorcovej dóze, to trvá asi 45 minút. Čas sa výrazne líši podľa veľkosti, tvaru a materiálu nádoby (napríklad kovová forma na chlebíček alebo sklenená zapekacia misa), preto gelato často kontrolujeme, aby sa neroztopilo.

en.t: 905 g plums (about 1020 g whole), pitted and quartered (about 945 ml)
200 g sugar
1 tbsp (15 ml) light corn syrup
1/4 tsp (0.8 g) kosher salt
Lemon juice, if needed, to taste

1. Purée plums in a blender or food processor until smooth. Once pitted, 905 g of plums should yield 945 ml of purée. Add sugar and corn syrup and blend for 30 seconds. Add salt, blend to incorporate, and adjust to taste. If plums are very sweet, add lemon juice to taste, starting with 1/4 tsp (1.2 ml).

2. Strain purée and transfer to refrigerator; chill for 2 to 3 hours until very cold. Churn sorbet in ice cream maker according to manufacturer's instructions. Transfer sorbet to freezer to firm up for 2 to 3 hours before serving.

en.t: 225 g heavy cream

1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) rose water
4 large eggs (about 200 g)
125 g honey
1/4 tsp plus 1/8 tsp (1.5 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use about half as much by volume or the same weight
Toppings such as sliced fruit, toasted nuts, cocoa nibs, or shaved chocolate

1. Getting Ready: Line an approximately 23 × 13 cm loaf pan with plastic wrap or parchment, so that the bottom and sides have been covered completely (plastic is the easier liner, but will give the semifreddo a wrinkled appearance; parchment takes a little more effort, but keeps the semifreddo smooth).

2. Next, prepare a hot water bath in a wide pot or large Dutch oven, with a thick ring of crumpled tinfoil set inside (the foil should be high enough to reach above the water level, so that it will later prevent the stand mixer bowl from touching the hot water and the bottom of the pot). If the stand mixer bowl has a metal foot, use a glass or ceramic bowl instead, in which case the foil ring is not needed.

3. For the Semifreddo: Combine cream, vanilla, and rose water in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment, and whip until stiff. The time will vary depending on the power of a given mixer, so keep a close eye on the process. Transfer to a separate bowl or plate, then cover and refrigerate until needed. Rinse the stand mixer bowl and whisk, then wipe dry before re-using in step 5.

4. Combine eggs, honey, and salt in the bowl of a stand mixer (or in a glass or ceramic bowl, if the stand mixer bowl has a foot). Stir with a flexible spatula to combine. Place over the prepared water bath, so that the bowl does not touch the water, and adjust heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

5. Cook, stirring and scraping constantly with a flexible spatula, until warmed to 74 °C, about 10 minutes in a stainless steel bowl, or about 15 minutes if using glass or ceramic. If the process seems to be taking much longer, simply increase the heat; top the hot water bath up with more hot water if needed at any point. Once the mixture reaches 75 °C, transfer to a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment. Whip on high speed until eggs are foamy, more than quadrupled in size, and thick enough to briefly mound up like soft-serve ice cream when dropped from the whisk, between 5 to 8 minutes, depending on the mixer’s power. The bowl itself should also feel cool to the touch.

6. Working by hand, gently whisk in half of the prepared whipped cream. Once smooth, add the remainder, whisk briefly, then fold with a flexible spatula until well combined. Scrape into the prepared loaf pan, cover tightly, and freeze until firm enough to slice, about 8 hours or to an internal temperature of -18 °C.

7. To Serve: Place a platter large enough to accommodate the loaf in the freezer until cold. Invert the semifreddo onto the chilled platter, using the plastic or parchment paper to pull it free. Leave the semifreddo covered, and return to the freezer until time for dessert. Then, tug loose the plastic or parchment, and top as desired with macerated fruit, toasted nuts, sauces, or whatever you prefer. Let the semifreddo stand 1 to 2 minutes at room temperature, then slice with a chef’s knife dipped or rinsed in hot water between each slice. Serve immediately.

en.t: 2 Mexican vanilla beans, for the cajeta

1. Make the cajeta in 2 separate batches, each with half of the cajeta ingredients: Split each vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds (reserve them for another use). For each batch, combine 1 pod with the goat's milk, sugar, baking soda, and salt in a 4700 ml stainless-steel pot. Warm over medium heat, stirring occasionally with a heat-resistant spatula, until the sugar dissolves and the milk turns foamy and light, about 15 minutes.

2. Keep cooking at a gentle simmer, stirring and scraping the sides of the pot frequently (more often as it thickens), until thick, golden, and reduced to a thin, very jammy layer, about 45 minutes, and a spatula dragged across the bottom leaves a trail that stays open for 1 second. Remove from heat, discard the vanilla pod, and scrape into a heat-resistant, wide-mouth glass jar. If a batch weighs less than 355 g, thin it with a little milk or water. (Cajeta can be refrigerated for up to 3 months.)

3. For the ice cream: Whisk the milk, cream, and vanilla into 1 batch of cajeta. Refrigerate until cold, at least 4 hours or up to 1 week, then churn in an ice cream maker according to the manufacturer's directions. (It can be frozen for up to 1 month in an airtight container with plastic wrap pressed against the surface.)

4. For the whipped cream: Chill 85 g of the second batch of cajeta. In a stand mixer fitted with the whisk, combine it with the cream and salt; mix on low, then whip on medium-high to the desired consistency, about 5 minutes for stiff peaks (or whip by hand with a balloon whisk). Warm the rest of the second batch for drizzling.

5. Before starting, freeze parfait glasses until frosty. Divide ice cream into as many portions as you prefer, dunking the ice cream scoop in hot water from time to time to ensure a clean release. Drizzle each with a few tbsp of warm cajeta, then top with a generous dollop of Cajeta Whipped Cream. Sprinkle with salted popcorn or other topping and serve immediately.

21 g Dutch-process cocoa
1/2 tsp (2 g) baking powder
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) espresso powder, optional
1/2 tsp (3 g) table salt
4 tbsp (57 g) unsalted butter
85 g chocolate chips
149 g granulated sugar
1 large egg (≈50 g without shell)
3 tbsp (43 g) water
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
24 g freeze-dried mango
12 g freeze-dried raspberries
454 g heavy cream
one can (397 g) sweetened condensed milk
pinch of table salt
149 g granulated sugar
3 large egg whites (105 g)
1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) cream of tartar
1/4 tsp (1.5 g) table salt
1. To make the brownie base: Preheat the oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C) with a rack in the center. Line a 20 cm round pan with parchment or lightly grease.
2. In a small mixing bowl, stir to combine the flour, cocoa, baking powder, espresso powder, and salt. Set aside.

3. In a saucepan set over low heat or in a large microwave-safe bowl, heat the butter and chocolate just until melted. (If using the microwave, heat at 50% power in 20-second increments.) Stir with a flexible spatula to combine.
4. Add the sugar to the melted chocolate mixture and stir until fully combined, then add the egg, water, and vanilla. Whisk to combine.
5. Add the dry ingredients and stir until the batter is smooth. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and level the top.

6. Bake for 20 to 22 minutes, or until the center feels set and the edges spring back slightly when pressed. Remove from the oven and cool completely on a rack. (The brownie base can be made up to 2 days in advance; store, well-wrapped, at room temperature until ready to use.)

7. To make the ice cream filling: Using a food processor, blender, or mortar and pestle, blend/crush the freeze-dried mango into a fine powder. Set aside, then repeat the process with the freeze-dried raspberries. Keep the two powders separate.
8. In a stand mixer fitted with the whip attachment, combine the cream, sweetened condensed milk, and salt. Whip on high speed until stiff peaks form, about 1 to 2 minutes.
9. Transfer half the mixture (about 425 g) into a medium bowl. Gently fold the freeze-dried mango powder into the whipped mixture in the bowl until evenly incorporated.
10. To the remaining portion in the stand mixer bowl, fold in the freeze-dried raspberry powder until evenly incorporated.
11. Line a 1890 ml metal bowl that’s 20 cm across the top and at least 7.5 cm deep with plastic wrap, making sure the wrap overhangs the edge of the bowl by a few cm.

12. Dollop alternating scoops of the mango and raspberry filling into the lined bowl, which will create a colorful pattern when the Baked Alaska is sliced. Alternatively, you can simply layer one filling on top of the other. Once both fillings have been added, tap the bowl on the counter a few times to eliminate any air pockets and use an offset or flexible spatula to smooth the top.
13. Remove the fully cooled brownie base from the pan and invert it directly onto the ice cream filling in the bowl, removing the parchment if necessary.
14. Press gently to adhere the brownie base to the filling, then wrap the entire bowl in plastic wrap and freeze until solid, at least 8 hours or up to 1 week.
15. To make the Swiss meringue: When you’re ready to serve the Baked Alaska, fill a saucepan with 5 cm of water and bring to gentle simmer.
16. In a large heat-proof bowl or in the bowl of a stand mixer, mix together the sugar, egg whites, cream of tartar, and salt until combined.

17. Set the bowl over the pan of simmering water, and cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture reaches 70 °C on a digital thermometer, about 5 to 7 minutes. If you don’t have a digital thermometer, dip a small spoon into the egg white mixture to coat it. Carefully run your finger over the spoon, then rub your thumb and finger together (the mixture will be hot!). It should feel smooth with no grittiness from the sugar remaining. If the sugar hasn’t completely dissolved, return the mixture to the heat and continue to cook and stir for several more minutes before checking it again.
18. Remove the bowl from the heat and use the mixer’s whip attachment or an electric hand mixer to whip the meringue on medium-high speed until stiff peaks form, about 4 to 6 minutes.

19. To assemble the Baked Alaska: Unwrap the bowl with the frozen ice cream and brownie base and invert it onto a serving platter. Gently lift the bowl up to reveal the ice cream and remove the plastic wrap. (You may have to use one hand to lift the bowl and the other to hold the plastic wrap in place.) If the ice cream won’t release from the bowl, gently warm the base with the palm of your hand or a warm towel to encourage it to separate.

20. Using a flexible or offset spatula, dollop the Swiss meringue onto the ice cream and spread it evenly to completely cover the ice cream and brownie base (spread it all the way to the serving platter), creating decorative swirls and peaks as you go.

21. Using a baker's torch, toast the meringue: Hold the torch 15 cm away from the surface and ignite it. Continuously move the torch in small circles as you work your way around the entire Baked Alaska, toasting the meringue. (Continuous movement will help prevent any one place from taking on too much color.) If you don’t have a baker’s torch

22. Once toasted, serve the Baked Alaska immediately. For the cleanest cuts, dip a large knife into a container of hot water. Remove the knife, wipe it dry with a kitchen towel, then immediately slice the Baked Alaska. Continue dipping and wiping the knife for each additional slice before serving.
23. Storage information: Any leftover Baked Alaska can be wrapped well in plastic or placed in an airtight container and stored in the freezer for up to 1 week.

3. V hrnci na miernom ohni alebo vo veľkej mise vhodnej do mikrovlnnej rúry zohrievame maslo s čokoládou, len kým sa neroztopia. (V mikrovlnnej rúre zohrievame na 50 % výkonu po 20 sekúnd.) Premiešame pružnou stierkou, aby sa spojili.
4. K roztopenej čokoládovej zmesi pridáme cukor a miešame, kým sa úplne nespojí, potom pridáme vajce, vodu a vanilku. Prešľaháme metličkou.

6. Pečieme 20 až 22 minút, kým stred nie je pevný a okraje sa pri zatlačení mierne nevracajú späť. Vyberieme z rúry a necháme úplne vychladnúť na mriežke. (Korpus môžeme upiecť až 2 dni vopred; dobre zabalený ho skladujeme pri izbovej teplote.)

1. To Prepare the Molds: Place dome mold sheet onto a sheet pan. Using a pastry brush, paint melted, tempered chocolate evenly on surface of each mold cavity, making sure chocolate goes straight to the edge. Place molds into fridge to set.

2. To Prepare the Cake: Preheat oven to 180 °C (fan 160 °C). Make an X with butter on surface of a rimmed baking sheet, then line it with parchment. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with paddle attachment, cream butter and sugar on high speed until light and fluffy, scraping down sides of bowl periodically. Add eggs and yolks one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Sift dry ingredients together. Turn mixer down to low speed and add half of the dry ingredients, followed by half the buttermilk. Mix on low until just incorporated, then add rest of the dry ingredients and buttermilk and mix until just incorporated. Remove bowl from stand mixer and finish mixing by hand with a large rubber spatula. Pour batter into prepared pan and spread it out evenly with an offset spatula.

3. Bake cake for 15 to 20 minutes, rotating halfway through, until tester inserted into center comes out clean and cake begins to pull away from sides of pan. Allow cake to cool for 15 minutes in pan, then run paring knife around edges. Place a piece of parchment on cake, followed by an inverted sheet pan, then turn cake upside down. Gently peel back top parchment from cake and allow cake to rest for 10 minutes before punching out circles with round cutter the same size as mold cavities.

4. To Prepare the Mousse: In a large bowl set over simmering water, melt white chocolate. Add the 57 g of cream a little at a time, stirring until mixture becomes smooth and warm to the touch. Melt bloomed gelatin in microwave (stop every 15 seconds to check) and stir into chocolate mixture. In a separate bowl, whisk together egg yolks and salt, then gradually whisk it into chocolate mixture. Continue whisking chocolate mixture for 1 minute over the double boiler, then remove bowl from heat. Place bowl in fridge to cool to room temperature (mixture should be neither warm nor cold, about 20 minutes). Whisk firmed chocolate mixture to smooth it out. Stir 1/4 of the chilled whipped cream into chocolate mixture to lighten it, then gently fold in remaining cream.

5. To Assemble the Bombes: Place mousse in a piping bag and pipe it into each chilled chocolate mold, taking care to only fill just to the top. Place a raspberry or two into each bombe and smooth mousse over top. Place a circle of cake over each mold and gently press cake into mousse. Place sheet pan of molds in freezer and allow them to set for at least 4 hours.

6. To Make the Sauce: Place frozen raspberries and sugar in a saucepan over low heat, stirring occasionally. As raspberries begin to melt, stir to help break them up. When fruit begins to simmer, remove from heat. Press fruit pulp and juice through a fine-mesh strainer. Discard seeds and chill sauce.

7. To Serve: Place 1 tbsp of sauce onto each plate. Create a design by dragging the back of a spoon through sauce. Loosen edges of bombes, then turn each cavity inside out to unmold them. 2. Príprava piškóty: rúru predhrejeme na 180 °C (teplovzdušnú na 160 °C). Na plech s okrajom nakreslíme maslom kríž a vyložíme ho papierom na pečenie. V mise kuchynského robota s plochým miešadlom vyšľaháme na vysokej rýchlosti maslo s cukrom do svetlej nadýchanej peny; občas zoškrabeme steny misy. Po jednom pridávame vajcia a žĺtky a po každom dobre premiešame. Suché suroviny spolu preosejeme. Znížime rýchlosť na nízku a pridáme polovicu suchých surovín a potom polovicu skysnutého mlieka. Miešame na nízkej rýchlosti, len kým sa nezapracujú, potom pridáme zvyšok suchých surovín a skysnutého mlieka a miešame, len kým sa nezapracujú. Misu zložíme z robota a dokončíme miešanie ručne veľkou gumenou stierkou. Cesto nalejeme na pripravený plech a lomenou stierkou ho rovnomerne rozotrieme.

3. Piškótu pečieme 15 až 20 minút, v polovici plech otočíme, kým špajdľa zapichnutá do stredu nevyjde čistá a piškóta sa nezačne odďaľovať od okrajov. Necháme 15 minút chladnúť na plechu, potom prejdeme nožíkom po okrajoch. Na piškótu položíme papier na pečenie, potom obrátený plech a piškótu obrátime. Jemne stiahneme vrchný papier a necháme piškótu 10 minút odpočívať; potom vykrajovačkou s rovnakým priemerom, ako majú jamky formy, vykrojíme kruhy.

4. Príprava peny: vo veľkej mise nad mierne vriacou vodou roztopíme bielu čokoládu. Po troškách pridávame 57 g smotany a miešame, kým zmes nie je hladká a na dotyk teplá. Napučanú želatínu rozpustíme v mikrovlnnej rúre (každých 15 sekúnd skontrolujeme) a vmiešame do čokoládovej zmesi. Misu dáme do chladničky vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu (zmes nemá byť ani teplá, ani studená, asi 20 minút). Stuhnutú čokoládovú zmes prešľaháme dohladka. Vmiešame ¼ vychladenej šľahačky, aby sa zmes odľahčila, a potom jemne vmiešame zvyšok.

5. Skladanie bômb: penu dáme do cukrárskeho vrecka a nastriekame ju do každej vychladenej čokoládovej formy, len po okraj. Do každej bomby vložíme jednu či dve maliny a penu navrchu uhladíme. en.t: 1 1/2 gelatin sheets
100 g cornflakes, for the cereal milk
825 g cold milk, for the cereal milk
30 g light brown sugar (2 tbsp tightly packed), for the cereal milk
1 g kosher salt (1/4 tsp), for the cereal milk
4 g freeze-dried corn powder (2 tsp)
30 g light brown sugar (2 tbsp tightly packed)
1 g kosher salt (1/4 tsp)
20 g milk powder
50 g glucose (2 tbsp)
1. Make the cereal milk: Heat the oven to 150 °C (fan 130 °C). Spread the cornflakes on a parchment-lined sheet pan and bake until lightly toasted, 15 minutes. Cool completely.

2. Transfer the cornflakes to a large pitcher, pour in the milk, and stir vigorously. Let steep for 20 minutes at room temperature. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a medium bowl, wringing the milk out of the cornflakes with the back of a ladle without forcing the mushy flakes through. Whisk in the brown sugar and salt until dissolved. (It keeps in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.)
3. Bloom the gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.

4. Warm a little bit of the cereal milk and whisk in the gelatin to dissolve. Whisk in the remaining cereal milk, the corn powder, brown sugar, salt, milk powder, and glucose until everything is fully dissolved and incorporated.

5. Pour the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into your ice cream machine and freeze according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The ice cream is best spun just before serving or using, but it will keep in an airtight container in the freezer for up to 2 weeks.
6. Powdered gelatin can be substituted for the sheet gelatin: use 3/4 tsp (3.5 ml). In a pinch, substitute 18 g (1 tbsp (15 ml)) corn syrup for the glucose.
7. Instead of a whisk, use a hand blender to mix the ice cream base.

en.t: 1000 ml vanilla ice cream, freshly churned
Chocolate feuilletine: 87 g dark chocolate (66% or more), finely chopped; 1 g kosher salt; 94 g feuilletine (or any crisp wafer/biscuit/cracker); nonstick spray
Marshmallow: 24 g powdered gelatine; 101 g water; 410 g granulated sugar; 202 g light corn syrup; 65 g honey; 101 g water

1. Day before: chill a silicone mat on a tray in the freezer 30 minutes. Spread the soft ice cream in the 25 × 20 × 2 cm tray and freeze about 4 hours. Turn out onto parchment, cut 12 rectangles of 2.5 × 2 cm, cover and keep frozen.
2. Feuilletine: melt the chocolate in the microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring; add salt, then feuilletine until coated. Spread, cool, break up, cover and refrigerate.
3. Serving day: coat every side of each ice cream rectangle with feuilletine; refreeze. Set 12 lightly sprayed ring moulds on a silicone mat on a tray.

4. Marshmallow: bloom gelatine in 101 g water about 20 minutes. Boil sugar, corn syrup, honey and water on medium without stirring to 121 °C. Pour into the mixer, add the gelatine, whisk on low until combined, then medium-high 4–6 minutes until white and quadrupled.
5. Working fast while warm, pipe (2.5 cm opening) to fill each mould ¾, press in an ice cream rectangle, cover with marshmallow and level. Set 1–2 minutes, unmould and freeze about 2 hours.
6. Optional: smoke the sticks in a sealed bag with applewood smoke for 30 minutes.
7. Insert a stick in each s'more, torch the whole marshmallow surface from 7.5–10 cm, and serve immediately.
